limits: Static checks cover selected files and known syntax only.
Typecheck, browser interactions, visual comparison and human review remain necessary.
Pages compose components; business behavior and services stay in the consumer.

components.label: Button
components.description: An action triggered by mouse, touch or keyboard, with progress and result states.
howToUse: Write the label as the action it performs, with a verb: "Save changes", "Send invite".
Keep one `primary` button per area. Other actions in the same area use `secondary` or `ghost`.
Use `danger` only for an action that deletes or cannot be undone, and confirm it first with AlertDialog.
While the action runs, set `loading` (or `status="loading"`): the button shows progress and ignores new clicks. Use `status="success"` or `"error"` to show the result in the button itself.
Use `block` in narrow columns and on mobile, where the button takes the full width.
alternatives: Going to another page: Button with `href`, which renders a link, or NavCard.
An action with only an icon: IconButton.
Several actions grouped under one: SplitButton or Menu.

components.label: IconButton
components.description: Compact action shown as an icon, with a required accessible name.
howToUse: Use it for a frequent action that a known icon already says: close, edit, delete, more options.
Always pass `aria-label` with the action ("Delete invoice"); it is what a screen reader announces.
Put it next to what it acts on, such as the end of a row or the corner of a card.
Pair it with Tooltip when the icon is not obvious to everyone.
alternatives: The icon alone does not say the action: Button with text, with `leadingIcon` if you want the icon.
Main floating action on mobile: Fab.

components.label: ButtonGroup
components.description: Grouping of related controls; selection and events belong to the child components.
howToUse: Use it to join buttons that act on the same thing, such as align left, center and right, or zoom out and zoom in.
Give the group a `label` that names the set ("Text alignment").
When one button stays marked as active, control it with `activeIndex` and `onActiveIndexChange`.
Use `orientation="vertical"` in toolbars on the side of the screen.
alternatives: Choosing one value for a form: Segmented or RadioGroup.
Turning several options on and off: ToggleGroup.

components.label: SplitButton
components.description: Main action paired with a menu of alternative actions.
howToUse: Use it when one action is the usual one and a few variants of it are occasional: "Save" with "Save as draft" and "Save and close".
List the variants in `options`; the main side runs `defaultOptionId`, or the first enabled option.
Keep `loading` on while the action runs, as in Button.
alternatives: The options are equally common: Menu, or separate buttons.
Choosing a value, not running an action: Select or Combobox.

components.label: OAuthButton
components.note: Oito provedores; fluxo OAuth pertence à aplicação.
components.description: Sign-in buttons for Google, Facebook, LinkedIn, Spotify, GitHub, X, Apple and Microsoft. They compose Button/GoogleButton; the application implements the OAuth flow.
howToUse: Use it on sign-in and sign-up screens, one button per provider, stacked with the same width.
Pick the provider with `provider`; the label and the logo come with it.
Start the sign-in in `onClick` and keep `loading` on until the provider answers. Show the cancel or the error next to the buttons.
The button does not authenticate: your application runs the OAuth flow.
alternatives: Only Google: GoogleButton.
Connecting an account to an integration after sign-in: ConnectorCard.

components.label: GoogleButton
components.note: Botão de entrada: autenticação real pertence à aplicação.
components.description: Google sign-in action, keeping the provider's identity and the control's states.
howToUse: Use it for "Sign in with Google" when Google is the only provider, or the main one.
Start the sign-in in `onClick` and keep `loading` on until Google answers.
Use `block` on narrow screens, where it takes the full width like the other sign-in buttons.
alternatives: Several providers on the same screen: OAuthButton.

components.label: Fab
components.description: Main floating action, compact or with a label.
howToUse: Use it for the one action people take most on a mobile screen: new message, new task, add photo.
Keep one per screen, in the lower corner, above the content.
Pass an `icon` and an `aria-label`. Use `extended` with `label` when the icon alone is not clear.
alternatives: Several related actions from the same corner: FabMenu.
Desktop screens, where the action fits in the header: Button.

components.label: FabMenu
components.description: Floating action that reveals a set of related actions.
howToUse: Use it when the main action of the screen has three to five variants: new note, new photo, new list.
List them in `actions` with short labels, and give the closed button a `label` ("Create").
Handle the choice in `onSelect`.
alternatives: Only one action: Fab.
Places people visit, not actions: Sidebar or NavigationMenu.

components.label: DecisionActions
components.description: Related decision actions, with processing, done and unavailable states.
howToUse: Use it for the decision on one item: accept or decline, approve or reject, save or skip.
Handle the choice in `onAction`. While your server answers, set `state` to processing; when it confirms, to done.
Turn off an action that does not apply with `disabledActions`, and say why in `statusMessage`.
alternatives: Deciding item after item by swiping cards: DecisionDeck.
A single action: Button.

components.label: Input
components.description: Text input with label, help, prefixes and error messaging.

usage.reason: Erro fica junto do dado que precisa ser corrigido

howToUse: Use it for one line of free text: name, e-mail, link, amount.
Always give it a `label`. Use `hint` for the format expected ("Only numbers"), and `error` to say what is wrong and how to fix it.
Set the right `type` (`email`, `url`, `tel`, `number`): the mobile keyboard changes with it.
For a password, use `type="password"`: the browser hides the characters and can offer to save it.
Use `prefix` and `suffix` for fixed parts, such as a currency symbol or a domain.
alternatives: Several lines of text: Textarea.
Picking from known options: Select or Combobox.
Phone, postal code or verification code: PhoneInput, PostalCodeInput or Otp.

components.label: Textarea
components.description: Multi-line text input with label, help and error.

usage.reason: Erro fica junto do dado que precisa ser corrigido

howToUse: Use it for text that can take more than one line: description, comment, message.
Give it a `label`, and a `hint` with the limit or the tone expected ("Up to 500 characters").
Show `error` below the field, saying how to fix it.
alternatives: One line: Input.
A message in a chat, with send and attachments: IntentComposer.

components.label: Select
components.description: Native selection of one option, with groups, label and help.

usage.reason: Expõe valor atual sem exigir pesquisa

howToUse: Use it to pick one option from a short, known list: country, size, sort order.
Give it a `label` and start with the most common option selected, or with an empty option that asks for a choice.
Group long lists with `optgroup`.
The list that opens is the browser's own; on mobile it is the phone's picker.
alternatives: Long list where typing helps: Combobox.
Two to five options that should all stay visible: Segmented or RadioGroup.

components.label: Combobox
components.description: Search field and selection of one option, with keyboard navigation.

usage.reason: Campo e opções cumprem a mesma tarefa; digitação filtra a escolha

howToUse: Use it to pick one option from a long list, where typing a few letters is faster than scrolling: city, customer, product.
Give it a `label` and, when it helps, a `hint` saying what can be searched ("Name or tax ID").
Group long lists with `group` on each option, and add `description` or `avatar` when the label alone does not tell two options apart.
Turn on `clearable` when "no choice" is a valid answer.
Set `emptyMessage` to say what to do when nothing matches.
alternatives: Fewer than about seven options: Select or RadioGroup.
More than one choice: Multiselect.
A list of actions, not values: Menu or Command.

components.label: Multiselect
components.description: Search and selection of multiple options, showing and removing the choices.

usage.reason: Chips e contador representam o valor; quantidade visível depende do espaço

howToUse: Use it to pick several options from a long list: tags, people, cities.
Each choice becomes a chip in the field, with its own remove button. Limit how many show with `maxVisibleChips`; the rest becomes a "+N" count.
Use `listPlacement="overlay"` when the list must not push the content below.
Set `emptyMessage` to say what to do when nothing matches.
alternatives: Only one choice: Combobox.
Up to about six options that fit on screen: Checkbox list or ToggleGroup.

components.label: Checkbox
components.description: Independent choice, with label, description and selected or disabled states.
howToUse: Use it for an option that can be on or off regardless of the others: accept terms, receive news, one item of a list.
Write the `label` as the statement that becomes true when marked ("Send me the weekly summary").
Use `description` for the consequence, and `boxed` when each option is a row the person compares.
The change only takes effect when the form is saved.
alternatives: Only one option of the group can be chosen: RadioGroup.
A setting that takes effect right away: Switch.

components.label: RadioGroup
components.description: Set of mutually exclusive alternatives, with labels and descriptions.

usage.need: Uma opção entre poucas alternativas sempre visíveis
usage.reason: Seleção exclusiva; não usar ToggleGroup para simular essa garantia

howToUse: Use it when only one of a few options can be chosen and the person needs to see all of them to decide: plan, delivery method, visibility.
Give the group a `label` with the question, and each option a short label, with a description when the difference is not obvious.
Start with the safest or most common option selected.
alternatives: Several options can be on at once: Checkbox.
Seven or more options: Select or Combobox.
Choices with image or price that work like cards: ChoiceCard.

components.label: Switch
components.description: Toggle of a preference between on and off.
howToUse: Use it for a setting that takes effect as soon as it changes: notifications, dark mode, auto-save.
Write the `label` as the thing being turned on ("E-mail notifications"), not as a question.
Save the change in `onChange`. If saving fails, switch it back and say why.
alternatives: The change only counts after the person saves the form: Checkbox.
An action that deletes or cannot be undone: Button with confirmation.

components.label: Segmented
components.description: Choice between related alternatives shown in a segmented control.

usage.need: Uma opção entre poucas alternativas sempre visíveis
usage.reason: Seleção exclusiva; não usar ToggleGroup para simular essa garantia

howToUse: Use it to switch between two to five views or modes of the same content: day, week and month; list and grid.
Keep labels short and of similar length. With `iconOnly`, the labels become the accessible names and tooltips.
Give the group a `label` that names what changes ("Period").
alternatives: More than five options: Select.
Several options on at once: ToggleGroup.
Separate sections with different content: Tabs.

components.label: ToggleGroup
components.description: A set of independent toggles with multiple values; for exclusive choice, use Segmented or RadioGroup.

usage.reason: API de múltiplos valores (`string[]`); cada botão liga/desliga sua opção

howToUse: Use it to turn on several filters or formats that stay visible: bold, italic and underline; critical, warnings and info.
Each button shows whether it is on; the value is the list of options on.
Give the group a `label` that names the set ("Severity").
alternatives: Only one option at a time: Segmented or RadioGroup.
Many options: Multiselect.

components.label: Range
components.description: Selection of a numeric range with two bounds and keyboard support.
howToUse: Use it to pick a range between two values: price, distance, area.
Give it a `label` and format the values with `formatValue` ("R$ 200", "5 km").
Add `histogram` to show how many results fall in each part of the range, and `ticks` for reference marks.
Use `fixedMinimum` when only the upper end changes, such as a radius from zero.
alternatives: One value: Slider.
An exact number that people type: Input with `type="number"`.

components.label: Slider
components.description: Pick a numeric value by dragging, track or keyboard.
howToUse: Use it for a value where the position matters more than the exact number: volume, opacity, intensity.
Give it a `label`; use `hideLabel` in compact bars, where the name stays only for screen readers.
Use `marks` when only a few steps are valid (1 to 5), and `ticks` to name the ends ("Shallow", "Deep").
alternatives: Two ends: Range.
An exact number: Input with `type="number"`.

components.label: Otp
components.description: Verification code input, with multiple slots and paste support.
howToUse: Use it for the code sent by SMS, e-mail or an authenticator app.
Set `length` to the size of the code, and `groupSize` to split long codes ("392 114").
Verify in `onComplete`, which fires when the last digit is filled. Show `error` when the code is wrong, and a resend link below.
Your application sends and checks the code, and controls expiry and attempts.
alternatives: A password or any free text: Input.

components.label: PhoneInput
components.description: Phone input with country selection, international code and formatting.
howToUse: Use it for phone numbers that can come from more than one country.
Start with the country most people use in `country`, and limit the list with `countries` when only some apply.
The Brazilian format is applied as people type. Validate other countries in your application.
alternatives: A phone that is always from the same country, with no selector: Input with `type="tel"`.

components.label: PostalCodeInput
components.description: Postal code (CEP) input and lookup, with searching, result and error states.
howToUse: Use it on address forms, so the street, district and city fill in from the postal code (CEP).
Pass your lookup service in `lookup` and fill the other fields in `onAddressFound`.
The search runs when the CEP is complete and the field loses focus, or on the Search button. If it fails, people can still type the address.
alternatives: An address outside Brazil, or a free search for places: Input or Combobox.
Picking an area on a map: GeoAreaPicker.

components.label: Calendar
components.description: Calendar to pick a date or a range, with limits and navigation between months.
howToUse: Use it when the calendar stays open on the screen: booking, availability, a period for a report.
Use `mode="range"` for start and end, with `numberOfMonths={2}` so both fit side by side.
Block the days that cannot be chosen with `min` and `max`.
Set `weekStartsOn` and `locale` for the country of the people using it.
alternatives: A date inside a form, where the calendar opens from a field: DatePicker.
Days with available times: SchedulePicker.

components.label: SchedulePicker
components.description: Selection of available days and times, with summary and time zone.
howToUse: Use it to book a time: a visit, an appointment, a call. The person picks a day, then one of the times available that day.
Pass the free times your server computed, and mark the busy ones with `unavailable`. Limit the days with `minDate` and `maxDate`.
Set `timezone` whenever the person and the place can be in different time zones; the summary shows it.
Confirm the booking on your server before saying it is done: the time can be taken in the meantime.
alternatives: Only a date, with no time: DatePicker or Calendar.

components.label: ChoiceCard
components.description: Choice shown in a card, with single or multiple selection and explanatory content.

usage.need: Escolher cards com texto ou mídia
usage.reason: ChoiceCard exige o contexto do grupo; `single` usa uma opção e `multiple` aceita várias

howToUse: Use it for choices that need more than a label to decide: plans with price, delivery options with deadline, templates with a preview.
Put the cards inside ChoiceCardGroup and give the group a `label` with the question.
Use `mode="single"` when only one can be chosen, and `mode="multiple"` when several can.
Set `columns` by how many fit side by side; `columns={1}` stacks them on mobile.
alternatives: Short options that a label explains: RadioGroup or Checkbox.

components.label: FileUpload
components.note: Arquivos são tratados apenas neste navegador, sem envio a servidor.
components.description: File selection and preview, with validation, progress and removal.
howToUse: Use it to attach files to a form: documents, photos, spreadsheets.
Say what is accepted in `accept` and `maxSize`, and repeat it in `hint` ("PDF or JPG, up to 10 MB").
Turn on `multiple` when more than one file makes sense.
Your application uploads the files. While it does, pass `state` and `progress`; if it fails, show `errorMessage` with what to do.
alternatives: A voice message: VoiceRecorder.
Showing photos already uploaded: MediaGallery.

components.label: GeoAreaPicker
components.note: Seleção textual funcional. Provedor de mapa não conectado.
components.description: Select an area by radius or regions, with optional map integration.
howToUse: Use it when people choose where a search applies: a radius around a point, or a list of neighborhoods.
Pass the regions in `neighborhoods` and the center in `baseId`. Limit the radius with `minRadius`, `maxRadius` and `radiusStep`.
The map is optional: pass your map provider in `map`. Without it, the choice works by text and the slider.
alternatives: A full address: PostalCodeInput and Input.
Picking a few cities from a list, without radius: Multiselect.

components.label: Breadcrumb
components.description: Hierarchical navigation path, showing the current page.
howToUse: Use it at the top of a page that sits deep in a hierarchy, so people see where they are and go back up: Projects / Refy / Settings.
Each level except the last is a link; the last one is the current page.
Long paths fold the middle into a menu after `collapseAfter` levels.
alternatives: Switching between sections at the same level: Tabs or NavigationMenu.
Steps of a flow: WizardStepper.

components.label: Tabs
components.description: Related content organized in tabs with keyboard navigation.
howToUse: Use it to split related content of the same page into parts that people see one at a time: Overview, Activity, Settings.
Keep the labels short, in two or three words, and start with the tab most people need.
Use `variant="pill"` inside cards and panels, and `wrap` when the tabs do not fit on one line.
alternatives: Switching the view of the same data (list, grid): Segmented.
Going to another page of the app: NavigationMenu or Sidebar.

components.label: NavCard
components.description: Navigation destination shown as an actionable card.
howToUse: Use it for a destination that needs a line of context: a project, a settings area, the next page of a guide.
With `href` it is a link; without it, a button that runs `onClick`.
Mark the page people are on with `current`. Use `variant="dashed"` for "Create new…" at the end of a list.
Put an `Avatar` or icon in `leading`, and a count or role in `meta`.
alternatives: An action that changes data: Button.
Content with image to read, not a destination: ContentCard.

components.label: Pagination
components.description: Navigation between result pages, with current position and bounds.
howToUse: Use it below a list or table that shows one page of results at a time.
Pass the current `page` and the total `pageCount`, and load the new page in `onPageChange`.
After changing page, take the person back to the top of the list.
alternatives: A feed people scroll without counting pages: a "Load more" Button.
A table with built-in pages: the `pagination` of Table.

components.label: SettingsSubnav
components.description: Navigation between settings areas, with groups and the current section marked.
howToUse: Use it on the left of a settings screen, to move between its areas: Profile, Team, Billing, Security.
Split long lists with `groups`, and mark the area open with `activeHref`.
Pass your router's link in `renderLink`, so the navigation does not reload the page.
alternatives: Steps that must be followed in order: WizardStepper.
Sections of the same long page: TableOfContents.

components.label: TableOfContents
components.description: Anchor table of contents that follows the visible section of a document.
howToUse: Use it next to a long page, such as documentation or terms, to jump between its sections.
List the sections in `items`, in the order of the page, with the `id` of each heading.
Turn on `scrollSpy` to mark the section being read, and `sticky` to keep the list on screen while scrolling.
alternatives: Going to other pages: SettingsSubnav or Sidebar.

components.label: WorkspaceSwitcher
components.description: Selecting and searching a workspace, with management actions.
howToUse: Use it at the top of the sidebar when the same person works in several workspaces or companies.
Pass the list in `workspaces` and switch the data of the app in `onChange`; show an error if the switch fails.
Use `compact` when the sidebar is collapsed: only the avatar shows.
alternatives: The account of the person, with profile and sign out: UserMenu.

components.label: UserMenu
components.description: Account menu with identity and actions provided by the application.
howToUse: Use it for the account of the person signed in: profile, settings and sign out.
Put it at the end of the top bar with `compact` (avatar only), or at the foot of the sidebar with `side="top"`, showing name and e-mail.
Change the items in `entries` and handle them in `onSelect`. Signing out is your application's job.
alternatives: Switching company or workspace: WorkspaceSwitcher.

components.label: HelpMenu
components.description: Menu of help resources, documentation and support.
howToUse: Use it in the top bar to gather help: documentation, keyboard shortcuts, contact support.
Change the items in `entries` and open each one in `onSelect`.
alternatives: Help about one field: HelpField.
A guided first visit: GuidedTour.

components.label: WizardStepper
components.description: The steps of a flow, with current, done and pending states.
howToUse: Use it at the top of a flow split into steps that follow an order: sign-up, checkout, onboarding.
Pass the `steps` and the `current` one. By default people can go back to done steps but not skip ahead; `allowFutureNavigation` lets them.
Give the flow a `label` ("Create account"), which is announced with the progress. On narrow screens it turns compact by itself.
Check the fields of a step before moving on: the stepper does not validate.
alternatives: Questions asked one at a time: Questionnaire.
Areas with no order: SettingsSubnav or Tabs.

components.label: Menu
components.description: Contextual list of actions, separators and labels, with keyboard navigation; no nested submenus.

usage.need: Executar ações como editar, duplicar ou arquivar
usage.reason: Itens disparam ações; não representa valor de um formulário

howToUse: Use it for actions about one thing that do not fit on screen: the "more" of a row, of a card or of a header.
Write each item as a verb ("Rename", "Duplicate"), separate groups with a separator, and leave the action that deletes for last.
Open it from an IconButton or Button and handle the choice in `onSelect`.
It has one level only: no submenus.
alternatives: Choosing a value for a form: Select or Combobox.
Right-click on an area: ContextMenu.
Searching among many commands: Command.

components.label: Badge
components.description: Compact label to convey category, quantity or state.
howToUse: Use it for a short label next to something: state ("Paid"), category ("Design"), count ("12").
Choose the `tone` by meaning: success, warning, danger, info or neutral. Write the state in the text too, not only in the color.
Add `dot` for a state that changes, such as online or offline.
alternatives: Something people click to filter or remove: Chip.
A message that needs a sentence: Callout.

components.label: Chip
components.description: Filter or selection tag, with semantic tone and optional removal.

usage.need: Filtro de opção única acima da lista, em chips
usage.reason: Grupo de radio com uma parada de Tab e setas; Chip com `selectionMode="radio"` solto não tem teclado de radio

usage.need: Filtros independentes acima da lista, em chips
usage.reason: Cada chip liga e desliga com `aria-pressed`; o grupo dá o rótulo de campo

howToUse: Use it for filters people turn on and off above a list, and for choices shown inside a field.
Mark the active filter with `selected` and show how many items it has with `count`.
Use `removable` with `onRemove` for a choice that can be taken out, and update your list in it.
When only one chip of the row can be on, put the row in `ChipGroup` with `mode="single"` and a `label`: the group gives the arrow keys and one Tab stop.
For a row of independent filters with a name, use `ChipGroup` with `mode="multiple"`. Give each chip a `value`.
alternatives: A label people do not click: Badge.
The main action of the screen: Button.

components.label: StatusDot
components.description: Compact signal of a state, with label and activity indicator.
howToUse: Use it for a live state in little space: online, syncing, error, in a list or next to a name.
Always write the state next to it or in `aria-label`: the color alone does not say it.
Turn on `pulse` only for something happening now. It stops when the system asks for reduced motion.
alternatives: A state with a word: Badge with `dot`.

components.label: Callout
components.description: Contextual message with a semantic tone, content and optional actions.

usage.reason: Conteúdo continua disponível, sem sumir antes de ser entendido

howToUse: Use it for a message about the page or the section it sits in: a limit about to end, a change of rules, a tip.
Choose the `tone` by meaning, write a short `title`, and say what to do in the text.
Put the action in `action` ("Upgrade plan"). Use `dismissible` only when the message can really be ignored.
alternatives: A short result after an action ("Saved"): Toast or Snackbar.
A decision people must take before going on: AlertDialog.
The error of one field: the `error` of the field.

components.label: EmptyState
components.description: Empty state that explains the situation and offers a next action when it applies.
howToUse: Use it where a list or area has nothing to show: first visit, a search with no results, a finished queue.
Say why it is empty in the `title` and what to do in the `message`: "No invoices yet" / "Invoices show up here after the first sale".
Offer the next step in `action`: create the first item, or clear the filters.
alternatives: Content still loading: Skeleton.
Something failed: Callout with `tone="danger"`.

components.label: Skeleton
components.description: Temporary visual structure that stands in for the content while it loads.
howToUse: Use it in place of content that is loading, with the shape of what will appear: text lines, an avatar, a card.
Set `width` and `height` close to the real content, and `circle` for avatars, so the page does not jump when it arrives.
Mark the area that is loading with `aria-busy`.
alternatives: An action people are waiting for: `loading` on the Button, or Spinner.
Loading ended with no data or with an error: EmptyState or Callout.

components.label: ProgressBar
components.description: Progress of a task or usage of a quota, with tone and loading state.
howToUse: Use it to show how much of a task is done: upload, import, steps of a sign-up.
Pass `value` from 0 to 100, and write the number or the step next to it ("3 of 5").
Use `indeterminate` when the end is unknown. Use `tone="warning"` or `"danger"` when the value means trouble.
alternatives: Usage of a plan against its limit: UsageMeter.
A short wait inside a button or small area: Spinner.

components.label: UsageMeter
components.description: Resource usage against a limit, with a value and a visual state.
howToUse: Use it in plan and billing screens to show what was used of a limit: credits, storage, seats.
Pass `label`, `used`, `limit` and `unit`. Put the detail in `meta` ("8 analyses this month").
The color changes by itself at `warnAt` and `criticalAt`. Next to it, offer what to do when it is about to run out.
alternatives: Progress of a task: ProgressBar.
A number with a trend, with no limit: Stat.

components.label: Toast
components.description: Result notice with configurable action, dismissal and duration.

usage.reason: Feedback global temporário; não substitui campo de erro ou decisão obrigatória

howToUse: Use it for the result of an action that does not need a decision: "Invoice sent", "Copied".
Put ToastRegion once in the app and keep the list of toasts in your state; remove them in `onDismiss`.
Add an action when it helps, such as "Undo". The toast stays while the pointer or the focus is on it.
alternatives: An error in a field: the `error` of the field.
A message that must stay on the page: Callout.
A decision: AlertDialog.

components.label: Snackbar
components.description: Result message with an optional contextual action; position and duration are set by the app.
howToUse: Use it for a short result at the edge of the screen, with an optional action such as "Undo" or "View".
Your application decides where it appears and when it leaves; it does not close by itself.
Keep the text to one line and the action to one verb.
alternatives: Several messages that stack and close by time: Toast.
A message tied to a section of the page: Callout.

components.label: NotificationBell
components.description: Access to notifications, with the unread count and read actions.
howToUse: Use it in the top bar to show what is new for the person, with the count of unread items on the bell.
Pass the `items` from your server. Open the related page in `onItemClick` and mark everything read in `onMarkAllRead`, updating the items and the count.
Set `emptyMessage` for when there is nothing new.
alternatives: The result of an action just taken: Toast.
A full history of what happened: ActivityTimeline.

components.label: Tooltip
components.description: Short explanation of a control, shown on focus or hover.
howToUse: Use it to name an icon button or explain a control in a few words, shown on hover and on focus.
Keep `label` short. Add `shortcut` when the action has one ("⌘K").
Turn on `portalled` when the tooltip is cut by a container with scroll.
Nothing in it can be clicked, and on touch screens it may never show: keep important information visible.
alternatives: Content with links or buttons: Popover.
A preview of a person or item on hover: HoverCard.
Help for a form field: HelpField.

components.label: Popover
components.description: Contextual content anchored to a control, with controllable open and close.
howToUse: Use it for a small task attached to a button, that does not need the whole screen: filters, a short form, a color picker.
Control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`, and put the content in `content`. Give it a `label` that names the task.
The rest of the screen stays usable while it is open.
alternatives: A task that blocks everything until it is done: Modal.
A list of actions: Menu.
Text only, with no controls: Tooltip.

components.label: HoverCard
components.description: Extra information revealed on hover or focus of an element.
howToUse: Use it for a preview of a person, link or item when the pointer rests on it: profile, page summary, product.
Put the preview in `content`. Adjust `openDelay` so it does not open when the pointer just passes by.
The element that opens it must also work alone, such as a link to the full profile: touch screens have no hover.
alternatives: Content people need to act on: Popover.
A short label: Tooltip.

components.label: HelpField
components.description: Help tied to a field, with an explanation and optional deeper detail.
howToUse: Use it as the label of a form field that needs an explanation: a tax term, a rule, a field people often get wrong.
Write `label` in the person's words and `helpText` in one or two sentences. Link the field with `htmlFor`.
When the topic needs more, use `onLearnMore` to open a Drawer with the full explanation.
alternatives: Help for the whole app: HelpMenu.
Telling what is wrong with the value: the `error` of the field.

components.label: GuidedTour
components.description: Sequence of guidance anchored to interface elements.
howToUse: Use it to present a new screen or feature in three to five steps, each one pointing at a part of the interface.
Open it on the first visit and save in `onComplete` that the person has seen it. Let people close it at any step.
Point each step only at elements already on screen.
alternatives: Help that stays available: HelpMenu or HelpField.
A first-use flow that collects data: Questionnaire or WizardStepper.

components.label: Modal
components.description: Dialog over the interface, with title, content, actions and focus management.

usage.reason: Foco fica na decisão até confirmar/cancelar

howToUse: Use it for a short task that must be finished or cancelled before going on: edit a record, invite a person, confirm details.
Give it a `title` that says the task, and put the actions in `footer`, with the main one last.
Control it with `open` and `onClose`. Use `width` for wider content, up to a form with two columns.
When it closes, focus goes back to the button that opened it.
alternatives: Confirming an action that deletes or cannot be undone: AlertDialog.
Details people consult while still seeing the page: Drawer.
A long task with several steps: a page with WizardStepper.

components.label: Drawer
components.description: Side or bottom panel for content and actions related to the current context.

usage.need: Editar detalhes preservando contexto da tela
usage.reason: Painel lateral para uma tarefa contextual; continua sendo modal quando configurado assim

howToUse: Use it for details or editing that people do while keeping the page in sight: the record of a table row, filters, a cart.
Choose `side`: `right` for details, `left` for navigation, `bottom` on mobile, `full` for a screen of its own.
By default the page behind is blocked. Set `modal={false}` when people need to keep using it.
Put the actions in `footer`, which stays fixed while the content scrolls.
alternatives: A short task that interrupts everything: Modal.
A few controls attached to a button: Popover.

components.label: Command
components.description: Command palette with search, groups and shortcuts to run app actions.
howToUse: Use it as a search box for actions and pages of the app, opened by a shortcut such as ⌘K.
Group the `items` (Pages, Actions, Recent) and show the shortcut of each one when there is.
Run the choice in `onSelect`. Listen for the opening shortcut in your app and keep the normal navigation visible: not everybody knows the shortcut.
alternatives: Few actions about one item: Menu.
Picking a value in a form: Combobox.

components.label: Table
components.description: Data table with search, filters, sorting, pagination and content states.
howToUse: Use it when people compare the same fields across many records: each column is a field and each row is one record.
Align numbers and amounts with `align="num"`, so digits line up on the right.
Turn on `searchable` for long lists, and `filterable` on columns with a few repeated values, such as status or owner.
Mark `sortable` only on the columns people sort by, such as date or amount.
When a row opens a detail, pass `onRowClick` and `rowLabel`, which names the row for screen readers.
Show `loading`, `error` and `empty` in place of the rows instead of hiding the table.
On mobile, set `minTableWidth`: the table scrolls sideways instead of squeezing the columns.
alternatives: Records that move between stages: KanbanBoard.
A few items with image and text: ContentCard in a grid.
Thousands of rows on a server: search and paginate on the server, and pass only the current page to the table.

components.label: Charts
components.description: D3 charts: cartesian, radial, statistical, hierarchical, networks, flows and maps; accessible legends, axes, tooltip and data.
howToUse: Use it to show numbers that change or compare: sales by month, share by channel, distribution of values.
Choose the chart by the question: line for time, bars to compare, pie only for parts of a whole with few slices.
Always set `title`, the axis titles (`yTitle`, `xTitle`) and `formatY` with the unit.
Offer the data as a table next to it when people need the exact values.
alternatives: One number with its trend: Stat.
A score from 0 to 100: ScoreGauge.
Exact values to look up: Table.

components.label: Stat
components.description: Display of a value with optional label, change and trend.
howToUse: Use it for the main numbers of a dashboard or plan: revenue, active users, limit per minute.
Write the name in `label`, the number in `value` and the unit in `unit`. Explain the number in `description` when it is not obvious.
Show the change with `delta` and a small trend in `chart`. Your application calculates both.
alternatives: Usage against a limit: UsageMeter.
A score from 0 to 100: ScoreGauge.

components.label: ScoreGauge
components.description: Score indicator with bands, label and size variations.
howToUse: Use it for a score from 0 to 100 shown at a glance: quality, health, match.
Pick `size` by place: `sm` in table rows, `md` in cards, `lg` at the top of a page.
Set the bands with `okAt` and `warnAt`, and say next to it what the score measures.
alternatives: A number with unit and trend: Stat.
Progress of a task: ProgressBar.

components.label: Matrix2x2
components.description: Points distributed in four quadrants, with axes, labels and selection.
howToUse: Use it to place items by two criteria and see which quadrant each one falls in: impact and effort, risk and likelihood.
Name the axes with `xLabel` and `yLabel`, and each quadrant in `quadrants` ("Do now", "Plan").
Pass the `points` in order of priority; open the detail of the chosen point in `onPointClick`.
alternatives: Values over time: Charts.
A ranked list: Table with sorting.

components.label: ActivityItem
components.description: An event with author, time, content and context. Molecule shared by the feed and the compact version of ActivityTimeline.
howToUse: Use it for one event: who did what and when, such as "Ana approved the invoice, 2 h ago".
Fill `actor`, `title` and `timestamp`; add `description`, `badge` or `status` only when they change what the person reads.
Use `density="compact"` in side panels and small widgets.
alternatives: A list of events grouped by day: ActivityTimeline.
Milestones of a project: Timeline.

components.label: Timeline
components.description: Milestones of a journey with dates and a time axis. Alternating vertical or horizontal, with optional media and actions. For events by people and systems, use ActivityTimeline.
howToUse: Use it for the milestones of a journey: an order from purchase to delivery, a project from kick-off to launch.
Pass the `items` in the order they happen, each with date and title; add media or an action when a milestone needs them.
Use `orientation="horizontal"` for few milestones in a wide area; vertical works on mobile.
alternatives: Many events by people and systems: ActivityTimeline.
Steps the person still has to do: WizardStepper.

components.label: ActivityTimeline
components.description: Activity history grouped by date: author next to content, context and actions. ActivityTimeline also builds compact widgets. EventTimeline is a compatibility alias. For milestones of a journey, use Timeline.
howToUse: Use it for the history of a record: comments, changes and system events, grouped by day.
Pass the `events` with author and time; set `locale` and `timezone` of the people reading.
Show loading failures with `error` and `onRetry`, and an empty history with `emptyTitle` and `emptyMessage`.
For a small widget, use `density="compact"` and `groupByDate={false}`. In new code, import it as ActivityTimeline.
alternatives: Milestones of a journey: Timeline.
A single event: ActivityItem.

components.label: KanbanCard
components.description: Work card with composed opening, metadata and actions. The same molecule is used in the column and in the KanbanBoard drag preview.
howToUse: Use it for one work item on a board: title, owner, due date, tags.
Open the detail in `onOpen`, usually in a Drawer. Put quick actions in `actions`.
Inside KanbanBoard the drag handle comes from the board; alone, the card only shows the item.
alternatives: A full board with columns: KanbanBoard.
Content to read, with image: ContentCard.

components.label: KanbanBoard
components.description: Board with global or per-stage WIP, per-column colors and transition rules. Drag by the handle or use keyboard/menu. Column and toolbar actions are composition, with no built-in business rules.
howToUse: Use it for work that moves through stages: sales pipeline, tasks, hiring.
Pass the `columns` with their cards and save the moves in `onColumnsChange`. Open a card in `onCardClick`.
Set a limit per column with `wipLimit` and the allowed moves with `allowedTransitions`. Check them on your server too: two people can move the same card.
Each card can also be moved by its menu, without dragging.
alternatives: Comparing many fields of each item: Table.
Dates and deadlines: Calendar or Timeline.

components.label: ApprovalWorkbench
components.description: Reusable review area, with information, progress and decision actions.
howToUse: Use it for a queue of items reviewed one by one: documents to approve, submissions to check, claims to analyse.
Pass the `items`; the list stays on one side and the item in `activeId` opens in the panel. Change it in `onActiveChange`.
Your application decides and saves the outcome of each item.
alternatives: A decision on a single item: DecisionActions.
A list to browse, with no decision: Table.

components.label: Avatar
components.description: Visual identity of a person or entity, by image or initials.
howToUse: Use it to show who: the author of a comment, the owner of a task, the account signed in.
Pass `src` with the photo and `initials` as fallback; `alt` with the name when the name is not next to it.
Use `shape="square"` for companies and projects, and `seed` for a fixed color per name.
alternatives: Avatar with name and detail in a row: PersonCell.
Several people at once: AvatarGroup.

components.label: AvatarGroup
components.description: Stack of avatars with a visible limit, overlap and a count of extra participants.
howToUse: Use it to show who takes part in something in little space: members of a project, people in a conversation.
Pass the `items` in a stable order and limit with `max`; the rest becomes "+N".
Use `onOverflowClick` to open the full list, and `onItemClick` to open a person.
A screen reader announces each person as an image with the name, with a photo or with initials; with `onItemClick`, as a button with the name.
alternatives: One person: Avatar.
A list of people with name and role: PersonCell in a list or Table.

components.label: BrandLogo
components.description: Refy wordmark and symbol with sizes and display variants.
howToUse: Use it for the refy brand in headers, footers and splash screens.
Use `markOnly` where only the symbol fits, and `tone` for dark or light backgrounds. The symbol takes the main color of the theme.
For your product's brand, pass it in `brand` with an `aria-label` that names it.
alternatives: A person or company in a list: Avatar.

components.label: PersonCell
components.description: Identification of a person or entity for rows, lists and tables.
howToUse: Use it to identify a person or company in a table cell or list row: avatar, name and one line of detail.
Put the e-mail or the role in `secondary`, and a short mark such as "you" in `tag`.
Use `size="sm"` in table cells and `md` in lists.
alternatives: Only the picture: Avatar.
A row that opens something or holds a setting: SettingRow or NavCard.

components.label: Card
components.description: Content surface with spacing, header and elevation levels.
howToUse: Use it to group content about one subject on a surface: a summary, a form section, a chart with its title.
Open it with CardHeader for title, description and action. Use `elevation` 0 or 1 on pages and higher values only for things floating above.
When the whole card opens something, put a link or button inside it: the card itself is not clickable.
alternatives: A destination in a list: NavCard.
Content with image, facts and actions: ContentCard.

components.label: Accordion
components.description: Expandable sections that reveal content when their titles are triggered.
howToUse: Use it for content people read in parts and seldom all at once: FAQ, filters by group, sections of a long form.
Write titles that say what is inside, so people find the part without opening all of them.
Use `type="multiple"` when people compare parts, and `defaultValue` to open the most read one.
Use `variant="plain"` inside cards, where the outer border would repeat.
alternatives: Sections people switch between often: Tabs.
A single block that opens and closes: Collapsible.

components.label: CodeBlock
components.description: Code with syntax colors, monospaced font and copy of the original content.
howToUse: Use it for code people copy: install commands, examples, API keys.
Set `language` for the colors and `label` for the file name or the purpose ("Production API key").
Use `secret` for keys: the value stays hidden, shows only the last characters, and the copy button copies the full value.
alternatives: A word of code inside a sentence: `<code>`.
Text people edit: Textarea.

components.label: ContentCard
components.description: Content card with media, information and actions, in different compositions.
howToUse: Use it for items people browse and compare by picture and facts: listings, products, places, courses.
Fill `title`, `media` and a few `facts`; add `badges`, `summary` or `matchScore` when they help decide.
Choose `layout` by place: vertical in grids, horizontal in lists. Put the actions in `actions`.
In new code, import it as ContentCard.
alternatives: A destination with one line of context: NavCard.
Deciding on items one at a time: DecisionDeck.

components.label: Coverflow
components.note: Exploração finita por conteúdo visual. Ativação e integração pertencem à aplicação.
components.description: Finite browsing of visual content with selection by identity, navigation, gesture and explicit activation.
howToUse: Use it to browse a finite set of covers or visual references and pick one: albums, themes, templates.
Draw each item with `renderItem` using only image and text: links and buttons inside it do not work.
Selecting moves the item to the center (`onSelectionChange`); opening it is a separate step (`onActivate`).
alternatives: A long list to read: a list or a grid of ContentCard.
Slides that people only go through: Carousel.

components.label: MediaGallery
components.description: Media display with aspect ratios, navigation and loading or error states.
howToUse: Use it for the photos of one item: a listing, a product, a place.
Set `aspectRatio` so the area keeps its size while loading, and `fit` to crop or show the whole picture.
Show `loading` while the photos arrive, and `errorMessage` with `onRetry` when they fail. In new code, import it as MediaGallery.
alternatives: Different content in slides: Carousel.
One fixed image: AspectRatio with an ``.

components.label: DecisionDeck
components.description: Sequence of decision cards with navigation, gestures and explicit actions.
howToUse: Use it to decide on items one at a time, like or skip: candidates, listings, suggestions.
Save each decision in `onAction`. The buttons do the same as the gesture, so people who do not swipe can decide too.
Offer to start over in `onReset` when the cards end. In new code, import it as DecisionDeck.
alternatives: Slides with no decision: Carousel.
Comparing several items side by side: a grid of ContentCard.

components.label: VoiceRecorder
components.note: Simulação de estados e duração, sem capturar áudio ou solicitar microfone.
components.description: Controlled interface for recording, pause, error and a text alternative; capture, permissions and transcription are wired by the app.

usage.reason: O componente controla apresentação/estados; MediaRecorder/Web Speech e permissões pertencem à aplicação

howToUse: Use it where people can speak instead of typing: a voice note, a search by voice, a message.
Your application records, asks for the microphone and transcribes. Pass the `state`, the `duration` and the `level` it reads.
Show the `transcript` for review before sending, and offer typing with `onUseFallback` when the microphone fails.
alternatives: Attaching an existing audio file: FileUpload.
A request with text and voice together: IntentComposer.

components.label: IntentComposer
components.note: Fluxo simulado de entrada e resposta, sem serviço de IA.
components.description: Composing a request, with suggestions and processing states.
howToUse: Use it as the box where people describe what they want in their own words, by text or voice: a search, an order, a question to an assistant.
Offer `examples` of good requests and the `filters` that narrow it. Handle the request in `onSubmit`.
While your service processes, set `state`; then show what was understood in `understoodSummary`, with a way to edit.
The component does not run AI: your application interprets the text.
alternatives: A plain form field: Input or Textarea.
Messages of a conversation: Message and MessageScroller.

components.label: Kbd
components.description: Visual representation of a key or shortcut combination.
howToUse: Use it to write a key or a shortcut in text, menus and tooltips: ⌘K, Esc, Enter.
One Kbd per key; join combinations with "+" between them.
It only shows the key: your application listens for the shortcut.
alternatives: Code people copy: CodeBlock.

components.label: AppShell
components.description: Application structure combining side navigation, top bar and content area.
howToUse: Use it as the frame of an app: sidebar on the left, top bar and the content of the page.
Configure the sidebar in `sidebar` and the top bar in `topbar`; the page goes in `children`.
Turn on `responsiveSidebar` so the sidebar becomes a drawer on mobile. Limit the reading width with `contentMaxWidth`.
alternatives: A public site page: Hero, Section and SiteFooter.

components.label: Sidebar
components.description: The app's side navigation, with expanded, compact and collapsed versions.
howToUse: Use it for the main places of an app, always visible on the side: Home, Projects, Reports, Settings.
Split items into `groups`, mark the page open with `activeId`, and put the main creation action in `cta` ("New project").
Use `workspaces` to switch companies at the top, and `account` for the person at the foot.
alternatives: Areas inside a settings page: SettingsSubnav.
A site with few pages: NavigationMenu.

components.label: Topbar
components.description: Top bar with path, search, tabs or segments and slots for actions; notifications, help and account are compositions by the consumer.
howToUse: Use it at the top of each app page: where the person is, search, and the global actions.
Show the path in `crumbs`, open the search in `onSearchClick`, and switch views with `tabs` or `segments`.
Put NotificationBell, HelpMenu and UserMenu in `actions`.
alternatives: The title and actions of one page: PageHeader.

components.label: PageHeader
components.description: Page header with title, description, path and contextual actions.
howToUse: Use it at the top of each page: the title, a line that says what the page is for, and the main actions.
The `title` becomes the page's only `<h1>`. Put the description in `lead` and the actions in `actions`, with at most one primary.
Pass a Breadcrumb in `breadcrumb` on deep pages, and context in `eyebrow` ("Team · Settings").
alternatives: A section inside the page: SectionHeader.
The opening of a public site: Hero.

components.label: SectionHeader
components.description: Section title with count, description and optional action.
howToUse: Use it to open each section of a page: "Members", "Recent invoices", "API keys".
The `title` becomes an `<h2>`. Show how many items there are in `count` and put a link or small button in `action` ("Manage").
Give it an `id` when the page has a TableOfContents. Use `rule` on dashboards.
alternatives: The top of the page: PageHeader.

components.label: Hero
components.description: A page's first fold with title, accent, lead and actions; the composition comes from the theme.
howToUse: Use it for the first screen of a public page: the main title, one sentence and the main actions.
Write the `title` as the promise of the page, the `lead` as the proof in one sentence, and put one primary and one secondary action in `actions`.
The layout comes from the theme: switching the theme changes the hero without code.
alternatives: The title of an app screen: PageHeader.

components.label: Section
components.description: Page block with text and proof side by side, stacked or in the theme's columns.
howToUse: Use it for each block of a public page: an argument with its proof, such as text next to an image, a demo or numbers.
Put the proof in `aside`. Use `layout="split"` for side by side, and `reverse` to alternate sides down the page.
On mobile the parts stack, and screen readers always read the text first.
alternatives: Data grids inside an app: Table or Card.

components.label: DeviceFrame
components.description: Browser or phone frame with the live page at the device's real width.
howToUse: Use it to show a page working inside a browser window or a phone, at the real width of the device.
Pass the page in `src` with a `frameTitle`, and the device size in `viewport`; it scales to fit.
The page inside does not react to clicks. Offer a link to open it for real.
alternatives: A plain screenshot with no frame: an `` in AspectRatio.

components.label: SiteFooter
components.description: Site footer with brand, link columns and credits.
howToUse: Use it at the end of public pages: brand, link columns, credits and legal notes.
Give each column a title; each one becomes a navigation named by it. Links to other sites open in a new tab and show ↗.
Put language and color mode in `settings`.
alternatives: Navigation inside an app: Sidebar.

components.label: Divider
components.description: Visual separation between content groups, with optional orientation and label.
howToUse: Use it to separate groups of content that have no title of their own, such as blocks in a menu or a form.
Use `label` for a choice between paths ("or"), and `orientation="vertical"` between items on one line.
alternatives: A group with a name: SectionHeader.
Space alone separates well enough: no divider.

components.label: StickyBar
components.description: Action bar tied to the context, kept during scrolling.
howToUse: Use it to keep the context and the actions of a long page in view while scrolling: the item open, its state, Save.
Show it with `visible` once the original header leaves the screen. Fill `title`, `status` and `actions`.
alternatives: Save and cancel at the end of a form: StickyFooter.

components.label: StickyFooter
components.description: Persistent footer with actions and information provided by the application; does not validate forms.
howToUse: Use it at the bottom of long forms, so Save and Cancel stay in reach.
Put the state in `start` ("Unsaved changes", "2 errors"), and the buttons on the right.
Your form validates and blocks Save when needed.
alternatives: Context and actions at the top: StickyBar.

components.label: SettingRow
components.description: Settings row with description, state and an associated action or control.
howToUse: Use it for each item of a settings page: a preference, a connected account, a session, an API key.
Write the `title` and a short `description`; put the detail (e-mail, date, masked key) in `meta`.
Put the control in `actions` (Switch, Button). Or make the whole row a link with `href`, with no controls inside.
alternatives: A destination card in a list: NavCard.
An integration with connect and disconnect: ConnectorCard.

components.label: PlanCard
components.description: Comparable presentation of a plan, with features, price and a choose action.
howToUse: Use it side by side to compare plans on a pricing or upgrade page.
Fill `name`, `price`, `period` and the `features`, in the same order in every card.
Mark the recommended plan with `highlighted` and the current one with `current`, which turns off its button.
Choosing only starts the change: your application confirms and charges.
alternatives: The payment method and next charge: BillingCard.
Usage against the plan limit: UsageMeter.

components.label: BillingCard
components.note: Dados fictícios. Nenhuma cobrança é realizada.
components.description: Billing summary and payment method, with actions provided by the application.
howToUse: Use it on the billing page: the payment method, the state of the subscription and the next charge.
Show only the last digits in `lastDigits`, never the full card. Put the state in `status` with a Badge.
Put "Change card" and "View invoices" in `actions`. The card data is collected by your payment provider.
alternatives: Comparing plans: PlanCard.

components.label: ConnectorCard
components.note: Exemplo visual de integração, sem conectar contas.
components.description: State of a connection or integration, with options to connect, manage or remove.
howToUse: Use it on integrations pages: one card per service, with its state and what it does.
Put the service logo in `logo`, the state in `status`, and "Connect" or "Configure" in `actions`.
Use `locked` with `lockHint` when the plan does not include the integration; keep the upgrade button working.
Your application runs the sign-in with the service.
alternatives: Signing in to the app with an account: OAuthButton.

components.label: DangerZone
components.note: Ações demonstrativas, sem excluir dados reais.
components.description: Area for sensitive actions, with explanation and callbacks; the application provides the confirmation before running.
howToUse: Use it at the end of a settings page for actions that delete or cannot be undone: delete project, transfer ownership.
Say what is lost in each action, in plain words.
Each button opens an AlertDialog before running: the zone does not confirm by itself.
alternatives: The confirmation itself: AlertDialog.

components.label: AlertDialog
components.description: Confirmation of an important action, with explicit confirm or cancel options.
howToUse: Use it to confirm an action that deletes, charges or cannot be undone.
Write the `title` as a question with the object ("Delete project Refy?") and say what is lost in the text.
Name the button with the action (`confirmLabel` "Delete"), never "OK". Use `destructive` for deletion.
While your server runs the action, set `pending`; show the error in the dialog if it fails.
alternatives: A task with a form: Modal.
An action that can be undone: run it and offer "Undo" in a Toast.

components.label: AspectRatio
components.description: Container that keeps the aspect ratio of images, videos and other media.
howToUse: Use it to keep the shape of an image, video or map while it loads and on every screen width: 16:9 video, square cover.
Pass `ratio` (16/9, 1, 4/3) and the media as children.
alternatives: Several photos with navigation: MediaGallery.

components.label: Bubble
components.description: Bubble that shows a piece of a conversation and identifies its source.
howToUse: Use it for one piece of a conversation: a message, a quick reply, a system notice in a chat.
Set `side` to tell who speaks: the person on one side, the other party on the other.
alternatives: A message with author, time and state: Message.

components.label: Carousel
components.description: Sequence of navigable content, with position indicator and forward controls.
howToUse: Use it for a few slides that people go through in order: highlights, onboarding screens, testimonials.
Give it a `label` and keep each slide readable on its own. It does not move by itself.
Control the position with `index` and `onIndexChange` when the page needs to know it.
alternatives: Deciding on each item: DecisionDeck.
Photos of one item: MediaGallery.
Content people compare: a grid.

components.label: Collapsible
components.description: Area that toggles content visibility through an expand control.
howToUse: Use it for one block that people open only when they need it: advanced options, details of an order, the rest of a long text.
Write a `title` that says what is inside ("Advanced options"). Start it open with `defaultOpen` when most people need it.
alternatives: Several blocks of the same kind: Accordion.

components.label: ContextMenu
components.description: Context menu triggered on a specific area or item.
howToUse: Use it for the actions of an item that people open with a right-click or a long press: a file, a card, a table row.
Pass the actions in `entries`, handle them in `onSelect`, and name the area with `label`.
Offer the same actions in a visible place too, such as a Menu on the item: many people never right-click.
alternatives: A visible "more" button: Menu.

components.label: DatePicker
components.description: Date selection by button and calendar, with clearing; no free typing.

usage.reason: Botão com calendário e limpeza; formato digitado, parsing e validação textual exigem outra composição

howToUse: Use it for a date inside a form: birth date, due date, start of a booking.
Give it a `label` and block the days out of range with `min` and `max`.
People pick the date in the calendar; there is no typing. For dates far away, such as birth dates, offer separate fields.
alternatives: A calendar always open on screen: Calendar.
Day and time of a booking: SchedulePicker.

components.label: Direction
components.description: Container that sets the reading direction, left to right or reversed.
howToUse: Use it around content in languages written right to left, such as Arabic and Hebrew.
Set `dir="rtl"`: the refy components inside flip. In your own layout, use start and end instead of left and right.
alternatives: The whole app in one language: set `dir` on the `<html>` tag.

components.label: Item
components.description: Content row with title, description, visuals and optional action.
howToUse: Use it for a row of a list: a file, a contact, a result, with title, description, picture and actions.
Pass `onClick` when the row opens something; mark the chosen one with `selected`.
Use `variant` without surface when the row sits inside a Card.
alternatives: Data compared in columns: Table.
A settings row: SettingRow.

components.label: Label
components.description: Form label tied to a control by the htmlFor attribute.
howToUse: Use it to name a field when you build your own control and it does not have a `label` prop.
Point `htmlFor` to the `id` of the field: clicking the label focuses the field, and screen readers read the name.
alternatives: Input, Select and the other fields already have `label`: use it.
A label with an explanation: HelpField.

components.label: Marker
components.description: Marking a piece of text with the theme's colors and shape.
howToUse: Use it to highlight a word or a short passage in a text: the term searched, the key part of a title.
The color and the shape come from the theme.
alternatives: A state that must be read: Badge.

components.label: Menubar
components.description: Bar of related menus, with options organized by purpose.
howToUse: Use it for a toolbar of menus in a tool-like app: File, Edit, View.
Pass the menus in `items` and handle the commands in `onSelect`. Name the bar with `label`.
alternatives: Navigation of a site: NavigationMenu.
One menu of actions: Menu.

components.label: Message
components.description: Conversation message with identity, content, time and optional actions.
howToUse: Use it for a message of a conversation with author and time: support chat, comments, an assistant.
Fill `author`, `initials` and `time`; set `side` to tell who speaks.
Your application sends and receives the messages.
alternatives: Only the bubble, without author: Bubble.
The list of messages with scroll: MessageScroller.

components.label: MessageScroller
components.description: Message area with scrolling and access to the latest messages.
howToUse: Use it for the area that holds the messages of a conversation and scrolls on its own.
Set `maxHeight` and a `label` ("Conversation with support"). When people scroll up, a button takes them back to the latest messages.
alternatives: Any content with its own scroll: ScrollArea.

components.label: NavigationMenu
components.description: Main navigation with groups and supporting content.
howToUse: Use it for the main navigation of a site or a simple app, at the top: Product, Docs, Pricing.
Pass the `items` and mark the page open with `activeId`. Group related pages under one item with a panel.
alternatives: An app with many areas: Sidebar.
Actions, not places: Menu.

components.label: Questionnaire
components.description: A sequence of questions with answer selection, navigation and completion.
howToUse: Use it for questions asked one at a time: onboarding, a short survey, a quiz to recommend something.
Pass the `questions` with their answers, and save the result in `onSubmit`. Keep it short: five to seven questions.
alternatives: A long form with sections: WizardStepper with fields.

components.label: Resizable
components.description: Split of an area into resizable panels.
howToUse: Use it for two panels side by side whose width people adjust: list and detail, code and preview.
Pass the panels in `first` and `second`, the start size in `defaultSize`, and limits in `min` and `max`. Save the size in `onSizeChange` to keep it.
On mobile, show one panel at a time.
alternatives: A fixed split: a CSS grid.

components.label: ScrollArea
components.description: Area with limited height and its own scrolling, keyboard accessible.
howToUse: Use it for a part of the page with its own scroll and a fixed height: a long list in a panel, a log, terms of use.
Set `maxHeight` and an `aria-label` that names the area. Avoid one scroll inside another.
alternatives: Messages of a conversation: MessageScroller.

components.label: Spinner
components.description: Visual indicator of an operation in progress.
howToUse: Use it for a short wait with no known end, in a small place: a button, a field, a card loading.
Give it an `aria-label` that says what is happening ("Loading invoices").
alternatives: Content with a known shape loading: Skeleton.
A known percentage: ProgressBar.

components.label: Trace
components.description: Expandable sequence of steps to show an operation's progress.
howToUse: Use it to show the steps of a process people want to follow or audit: what an assistant did, a deploy, an import.
Pass the `steps` with their state and result; each one opens to show the details and the code.
alternatives: A history of what people did: ActivityTimeline.

components.label: Prose
components.description: Typography for editorial content, including headings, paragraphs, lists, links and tables.
howToUse: Use it around long text written by people: articles, documentation, terms, release notes.
Headings, paragraphs, lists, links, quotes and tables inside it take the theme's type. Use `measure="text"` to limit the line to a comfortable reading width.
Clean HTML that comes from outside before showing it.
alternatives: Text people edit: Textarea.
